declaration.preface:
This Ethics Policy sets out the binding ethical principles and compliance obligations of Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH ("Prestige Promotion"). It defines qualitative commitments, detailed measures, and quantitative objectives.

The policy is based on the principles of the honourable merchant, the UN Global Compact, the German Criminal Code (StGB), the German Money Laundering Act (GwG), the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG), the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and applicable international anti-corruption standards including the UK Bribery Act 2010 and the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA).
declaration.declaration:
Prestige Promotion follows the principle of the honourable merchant and acknowledges its responsibility as a company operating in the highly regulated pharmaceutical co-packaging sector. All business activities are based on the following core values:

Prestige Promotion supports the ten principles of the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) covering human rights, labour, environment and anti-corruption, and commits to integrating these into its corporate governance. The company is actively reviewing formal accession to the UNGC.

The management of Prestige Promotion commits to:

Maintaining a strict zero-tolerance policy towards all forms of corruption, bribery, fraud, money laundering and unethical conduct — without exception and regardless of the position of the person concerned or the economic interest of the company

Providing the resources, governance structures and training necessary to implement and continuously improve the ethics and compliance programme

Exemplifying ethical conduct in all business activities and exercising the role-model function expected of management

Conducting an annual corruption risk assessment and integrating the results into the annual management review

Maintaining effective whistleblower and reporting mechanisms in compliance with the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG)

Ensuring regular communication of ethical obligations to all employees and relevant stakeholders

Reviewing and updating this policy at least annually, incorporating changes in law, and operational experience

Applying appropriate sanctions — including employment law and criminal law consequences — to any violations of this policy
declaration.scope:
This policy applies without exception to:

All employees of Prestige Promotion: full-time, part-time, fixed-term, casual workers, interns and apprentices

Management and all members of the leadership team, regardless of position

Temporary workers, external consultants and contractors acting on behalf of the company

Business partners, suppliers and service providers, to the extent contractually agreed

All business activities and sites of Prestige Promotion, worldwide and regardless of whether local laws impose less stringent requirements

Corruption: Prestige Promotion maintains an unconditional zero-tolerance towards all forms of corruption and bribery. This applies to all business activities, both domestic and international, regardless of local customs or market conditions. No financial or commercial interest justifies deviation from this commitment. Management exercises a role-model function and bears personal responsibility for creating an environment in which corruption cannot arise.
The following conduct is prohibited without exception:
Offering, promising, granting or approving advantages to public officials or business partners in exchange for preferential treatment in decisions, contract awards or supply arrangements
Demanding, accepting a promise of, or receiving personal advantages in exchange for preferential treatment in a supply arrangement or contract award
Facilitation payments of any kind, including to public officials
Kickback payments, covert commissions or payments to intermediaries where it is known or reasonably assumed that these will be used for bribery
Participation in bid-rigging arrangements or anti-competitive agreements with competitors
Covert payments via third parties (consultants, asset managers, agents) intended to circumvent anti-corruption controls
Any conduct creating the appearance of attempting to influence business or governmental decisions through improper means
Prestige Promotion conducts a formal corruption risk assessment at least once per year. The assessment covers:
Identification of company areas exposed to corruption risk, including purchasing, sales, supplier qualification, public contracts and regulatory interactions
Assessment of the likelihood of occurrence and extent of damage for each identified risk area
Determination and documentation of appropriate anti-corruption control measures
Derivation and approval of a corrective and preventive action plan (CAPA plan)
Submission to and approval by management as part of the annual management review (QMH Chapter 5.7)

All gifts and entertainment above threshold limits are recorded in the Gifts & Entertainment Register and evaluated annually. Gifts or entertainment during ongoing contract negotiations or tendering processes are prohibited.
Conflict of Interest: Prestige Promotion requires all employees to act in the best interest of the company at all times and to avoid situations in which personal interests conflict or could conflict with the objective fulfilment of their professional duties. All potential or actual conflicts of interest must be disclosed without delay. The company ensures that reported conflicts are assessed, managed and documented transparently and impartially.
A conflict of interest exists or may exist where personal interests could impair the objective fulfilment of professional duties. Examples include:
Business relationships with family members or close friends where the employee has influence over a relevant decision (purchasing, contracting, hiring)
Secondary employment or consultancy activities for competitors, customers, or suppliers of Prestige Promotion without prior disclosure and approval
Direct or indirect shareholdings in companies that are current or prospective business partners of Prestige Promotion
Receipt of personal benefits (gifts, invitations, financial advantages) in connection with supplier selection, contract award or procurement decisions
Participation in a hiring or performance evaluation decision where the employee has a personal relationship with the candidate
Use of confidential information obtained in the course of employment for personal financial gain or for the benefit of third parties

All employees are required to report potential or actual conflicts of interest to their line manager and/or the compliance function without delay, and before acting in any matter where a conflict may exist.

Employees in key positions — including purchasing, management, project management and senior quality roles — sign a formal annual conflict of interest declaration confirming disclosure of all known or potential conflicts.
The compliance function and management assess each reported conflict, determine appropriate management measures (recusal, oversight, transfer of responsibility), and document the outcome.
Employees are not disadvantaged for making good-faith disclosures; retaliation against employees who disclose conflicts is prohibited and will be treated as a disciplinary matter.
Line managers are trained to recognise indicators of undisclosed conflicts of interest and to manage disclosures with confidentiality and impartiality.
Fraud: Prestige Promotion maintains zero tolerance towards all forms of fraud, embezzlement, falsification of documents, manipulation of accounts, theft or deception — whether committed by employees, contractors or business partners. The company implements a robust system of preventive controls, detection mechanisms and response procedures to ensure that fraud risks are systematically identified and addressed.
The following conduct is prohibited without exception:
Falsification of documents, reports, invoices, contracts, test records, quality documentation, or any other business record
Manipulation of accounts, financial reports, inventory records or any system-generated data
Embezzlement, misappropriation or unauthorised use of company assets, funds or property
Submission of false expense claims, inflated travel cost reimbursements, or claims for work not performed
Deception of customers, suppliers, authorities or other stakeholders through false information, misleading statements or omissions
Theft or misappropriation of physical assets, intellectual property or confidential information belonging to the company, customers or business partners
Circumvention of internal controls, approval processes or segregation of duty requirements
Collusion with external parties to defraud the company or any third party

Four-eyes principle applied to all payment approvals, contract awards, purchase orders above defined thresholds, and significant financial transactions — two independent approvals required before execution
Defined and documented authorisation matrix specifying approval authority limits by role and transaction type; regularly reviewed and updated as part of the management review process
Segregation of incompatible functions: the person who initiates a transaction may not be the same person who approves and processes payment — enforced across procurement, accounting and logistics
Regular internal audits and self-inspections conducted in accordance with SOP-16.01, including unannounced spot checks of financial records, expense claims, inventory and document integrity

Data integrity controls in accordance with SOP-10.03 and SOP-10.04, ensuring that all quality-relevant and financial records are complete, accurate, traceable, contemporaneous, original and attributable (ALCOA+)
GMP-compliant batch record and documentation controls preventing unauthorised modification of pharmaceutical packaging records, serialisation data and quality system entries
Fraud awareness and prevention training for functions at elevated risk, including accounting, purchasing, logistics and warehouse management
Money Laundering: Prestige Promotion is committed to preventing any involvement — direct or indirect — in money laundering, the concealment of unlawfully obtained funds, or the financing of criminal or terrorist activities. The company will not enter into, maintain or facilitate business relationships that serve to disguise the origin, ownership or disposition of illicit funds. All business transactions are conducted transparently, lawfully and with full accountability.
Accepting, processing or transferring funds where there are reasonable grounds to suspect that they originate from unlawful activities
Structuring transactions in a manner designed to avoid reporting obligations or regulatory scrutiny
Establishing or maintaining fictitious accounts, black funds or covert financial arrangements
Accepting unusual cash payments of disproportionate size or structure without adequate justification and documentation
Entering into contracts or business relationships with parties known to be associated with criminal activities or subject to financial sanctions
Issuing or accepting fictitious invoices, false invoice descriptions or payments without a legitimate commercial basis

Know Your Customer (KYC) — prior to entering into significant new business relationships, Prestige Promotion verifies the identity, business purpose and beneficial ownership of counterparties, with particular attention to politically exposed persons (PEPs), sanctioned parties and high-risk jurisdictions

Sanctions screening — all new and existing significant business partners are screened against applicable EU, UN, OFAC and national sanctions lists; screening is documented and repeated on a risk-based basis

Unusual transaction monitoring — employees are trained to identify and report red flags including: payments to or from unknown third parties; requests for unusual payment routes; unusually large or split cash transactions; payments without apparent commercial justification

Transparent payment procedures — all payments are made only to verified counterparties on the basis of proper documentation; payments to third parties on behalf of a business partner require additional approval and justification

Proper accounting — all business transactions are completely, truthfully and promptly recorded; no fictitious entries or transactions without economic substance are permitted; the four-eyes principle applies to all payment-relevant transactions

Reporting obligation — employees who detect or reasonably suspect money laundering activity are required to report immediately to management and/or the compliance function; statutory reporting obligations to competent authorities are fulfilled where required by law
Responsible Information Management: Prestige Promotion is committed to the responsible, lawful and ethical management of all information in its care — including personal data of employees, customers, business partners and patients; confidential business information; intellectual property; and GMP-relevant quality records. The company respects the privacy rights of all individuals, protects confidential information entrusted to it, maintains data integrity across all systems, and responds promptly and transparently to data protection incidents.

All personal data — including employee records, customer contact data, patient-related information, and supplier data — is processed strictly in accordance with the GDPR, the BDSG and internal data protection policies
Personal data is collected only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; data minimisation is applied — only data necessary for the defined purpose is collected and retained
All employees with access to personal data receive mandatory GDPR awareness training upon induction and annually thereafter; training is documented in the training management system

Data subjects' rights — including access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection — are respected and can be exercised through documented procedures; requests are processed within statutory deadlines
Personal data is shared with third parties only where a lawful basis exists; data processing agreements are in place with all relevant third-party processors

Internal company data — including commercial strategy, customer lists, pricing, process documentation and quality system content — is classified and protected in accordance with SOP-03.03, with access granted strictly on a need-to-know basis

Confidential information belonging to customers, business partners and suppliers is treated with the same level of protection as internal confidential data; non-disclosure obligations are contractually documented
Intellectual property of Prestige Promotion and of business partners and customers is respected; unauthorised reproduction, disclosure or use is prohibited
Employees leaving the company are required to return all company devices, data and confidential materials; access rights are revoked promptly upon termination

All GMP-relevant records — including batch records, test results, serialisation data, quality system entries, deviation reports and change control documentation — comply with ALCOA+ principles: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring and Available

Data integrity controls defined in SOP-10.03 and SOP-10.04 are applied across all systems — electronic and paper-based — used in the production, storage and release of pharmaceutical and medical device products
Unauthorised modification, deletion or falsification of GMP records is treated as a critical compliance violation subject to immediate escalation, root cause investigation and CAPA
Audit trails in electronic systems used for quality-critical processes are activated, protected and reviewed as required by EU GMP Annex 11

Internal IT systems and data repositories are protected through role-based access controls, password policies, and appropriate technical and organisational security measures proportionate to the risk of the data held

In the event of a personal data breach, the internal escalation procedure is immediately initiated; reportable breaches are notified to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours in accordance with GDPR Article 33, and to affected individuals where required
A mandatory reporting obligation applies to all employees who become aware of an actual or suspected data breach, data loss, or unauthorised access to company systems or confidential information

policy.monitoring:
Prestige Promotion has established an internal reporting office in compliance with the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG) and the underlying EU Whistleblower Protection Directive. All employees, external partners and other parties may report indications of possible violations of this policy, applicable law or ethical standards — regardless of employment status, nationality or position.

Non-retaliation: whistleblowers who make reports in good faith will not be disadvantaged, dismissed, transferred, demoted or otherwise adversely treated; any retaliation constitutes a violation of this policy and the HinSchG

Confidentiality: the identity of the whistleblower is protected in strict confidence; anonymous reports are accepted and processed equally

Impartiality: the reporting office acts independently; it does not report to the person or function against whom a complaint is made

Feedback: acknowledgement of receipt provided within 7 days; feedback on follow-up measures within 3 months from acknowledgement

Documentation: all reports are documented and retained for a minimum of 3 years, or longer if required by applicable law or ongoing proceedings

The reporting procedure, contact information and protection guarantees are provided in at least German and English to ensure accessible reporting for all employees regardless of language background.

Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all employees. Prestige Promotion ensures that all persons covered by this policy have the knowledge and awareness necessary to fulfil their obligations.

Semi-annual review of quantitative targets by QMO / Compliance

Annual review of all entries; verification of compliance with thresholds and approvals

In the event of incidents, complaints, new legislation, or supply chain findings
